lines.trans: Doctor Tenenbaum is listening. What happened?
Yakov Grigoryevich, I have an urgent question for you.
There is a boy here, Lyokha. Speak with him.
Hello, doctor. I have osteochondropathy.
So how are they treating you?
They scheduled surgery for me.
Tell me, boy. Did a tick ever bite you?
Yes, a year ago. Then everything went away.
Well then, run along, boy! Arkasha, listen to me.
This boy has no osteochondropathy at all.
He has Lyme disease from a tick bite!
And he does not need surgery.
This condition is treated with medication.
Thank you, doctor! I understood everything.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

examples.text: У него боррелиоз от укуса клеща.
examples.trans: He has Lyme disease from a tick bite.
Lyme disease is treated with antibiotics.

examples.text: У него боррелиоз от укуса клеща!
examples.trans: He has Lyme disease from a tick bite!

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
medical practitioner; often used as form of address

examples.trans: Doctor, I urgently need a cast.
It hurts, it hurts! It hurts very much, Doctor!

examples.text: Я умоляю вас, доктор! Это всё ради любви!
examples.trans: I beg you, Doctor! This is all for love!

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
This condition is treated with medication.

meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Did a tick ever bite you?
There are many ticks in the forest in spring.

examples.text: Скажи мне, мальчик. Тебя когда-нибудь клещ кусал?
examples.trans: Tell me, boy. Did a tick ever bite you?

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you will want to make up with your dad.

examples.text: Вы любили когда-нибудь? Смотрите, мэр стоит на коленях!
examples.trans: Have you ever loved? Look, the mayor is on his knees!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bite', paired with 'укусить'.

examples.text: Скажи мне, мальчик. Тебя когда-нибудь клещ кусал?
examples.trans: Tell me, boy. Did a tick ever bite you?

meanings.en: (colloquial) to lecture, to try to talk round
meanings.note: не надо меня лечить = don't lecture me

examples.trans: This doctor treats patients very well.

examples.text: Не надо меня лечить, хорошо? Я своё решение принял.
examples.trans: Don't lecture me, alright? I've made my decision.

лечиться.gloss: to undergo treatment, to be treated

meanings.en: to undergo medical treatment, be treated
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to undergo treatment, to be treated', paired with 'вылечиться'.

examples.trans: He is being treated in the hospital.
This condition is treated with medication.

meanings.note: used to address a child you don't know

examples.trans: This condition is treated with medication.
The illness can be cured with drugs.

meanings.note: два года назад = two years ago

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: That's what the operation is called.

examples.text: Ты посмотри на этих москвичей, лейтенант. А сами операции проваливают.
examples.trans: Just look at these Moscow types, Lieutenant. And they're the ones who mess up operations.

meanings.note: medical condition of bone and cartilage

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: понял? = got it?; понял = got it

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: about a feeling or pain: потом пройдёт = it'll pass
'Пройдёмте' = let's go, an official's polite order
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent, pressing').

examples.trans: This is a very urgent matter.

examples.text: Яков Григорьевич, у меня срочный вопрос к вам.
examples.trans: Yakov Grigoryevich, I have an urgent question for you.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bite, sting' in everyday Russian.
